editorial.headline: The Army Activity With No Foreign-Investment Route
editorial.standfirst: An Army-wide activity field with an unambiguous foreign-investment answer nationally—and no opening in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 84222 takes up the Army’s own working machinery: the full range of its administrative, operational and related activities. It is not limited to a single office function or operational task. The scope gathers those activities as one institutional field, allowing the administrative and operational sides to be read together. All named work belongs to that same field: administration, operations and other related activity. Civilian employees working within the Army environment are expressly included. The boundary is equally deliberate: members of the Army who are employed elsewhere or who hold a government position are excluded, with Army Headquarters given as an example. What remains is an activity defined by the Army setting and by work undertaken inside it, rather than by a loose occupational label.

That framing also explains why the scale question has no conventional commercial answer here. The record lists no business scale as open. It identifies a defined set of Army activities and includes civilian personnel working in that environment, while separately specifying who is excluded. There is therefore no stated scale pathway in the slim record to rely on; no business scale is named as open. That omission is substantive rather than decorative: the record provides no scale-based route. For readers assessing the classification, the disciplined reading is to stay with its stated scope: administration, operations and related Army activities, together with the exclusions that shape the edge of the field.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is closed. The PMA ceiling is 0%, so foreign ownership is not available under this activity; an open national route cannot be inferred from the breadth of its operational description. The record cites Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 for that position, and supplies no positive foreign-ownership percentage or open business scale. Bali supplies no different route. Its status is also closed, and a foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today. The Bali note describes a medium-high/high risk position and says it is not blocked by the provincial PMA moratorium, while directing verification for the particular address. That detail should be kept in its proper place. Address-specific verification does not turn a stated closed status into an opening: it calls for confirmation at the address while Bali remains closed in this record.
